caption:
Comment "GOOGLE" to get all these Free AI Vibe Coding Tools by Google.

While everyone's been losing their minds over ChatGPT and Cursor. Google has been quietly dropping over 10+ free AI coding tools. The best part? They're all free. No catch.

Start with Antigravity. It's Google's AI code editor. Works like Cursor. I recently asked it to build a simple dashboard app. Just typed: "Make a responsive e-commerce page with login." Boom. Full code. Preview. Ready to deploy. Like having a dev friend who never sleeps.

Then Google AI Studio. Perfect for quick AI apps. Drag blocks. Add Gemini. Seconds later? A chatbot or image tool. Think of it as Lego for prototypes. Fast. Fun. No code needed.

Next, Stitch. Their AI design tool. Upload a wireframe. Or describe it. "Clean fintech UI with dark mode." It spits out designs. Plus front-end code in HTML or React. Designers love this. Like magic for sketches.

Opal comes next. Mixes n8n workflows with no-code ease. Build AI apps. Use models like Veo 3 for video. Or Nano Banana for light tasks. Here's why people keep using it:

 1. Wires automations in minutes
 2. Handles marketing flows or ops
 3. No servers to worry about

Like n8n met a friendly builder.

Finally, Jules. The AI coding agent. Connect your GitHub. Tell it: "Add user onboarding. Run tests." It builds features. Fixes bugs. Manages the whole codebase. I tried it on my side project last week. Saved hours. Feels like a junior dev on your team.

That's five from 12. Others like Project IDX for cloud coding. Gemini Code Assist for your editor. Makani for workflows and much more

caption:
Comment "OPEN" to get this website,, which has free and open-source alternatives for popular paid AI tools and software. 

Many people keep paying for expensive tools and subscriptions without knowing they don’t have to. If you’re still paying, you might be throwing money away.

Here’s the deal: there’s a website that shows you free and open-source alternatives to nearly every paid tool.

The site is called OpenAlternative.co. It’s like a treasure chest for anyone looking to save cash.

You can find free options for popular tools such as:

- Cursor, a coding editor
- Photoshop, for image editing
- Canva, for design work
- Notion, for organizing your projects

And the list goes on.

I remember switching from a pricey design tool to a free alternative I found there. It took a bit of getting used to, but it worked well enough for my needs—and saved me a lot of money.

Think of it like trading a fancy coffee shop latte for a great cup brewed at home. You still get the boost, but your wallet stays happier.

Why pay every month when great tools are out there for free? Check out OpenAlternative.co and give a few a try. You might love what you find.
